T: The Little Family Just Got Bigger
D: A Manhattan family adopts a small, polite mouse as their second son, and the family cat is not having it.
P: Serve the meatloaf when Frederick tells Eleanor it's delicious.
S: Cocktail sausages rolled in puff pastry and baked golden, for the whole Little family.

Heat the oven to 200C. Cut 2 thawed sheets of puff pastry into 24 strips. Wrap each of 24 cocktail sausages in a strip, seam side down on a lined tray, and brush with beaten egg. Bake 18 to 20 minutes until puffed and golden. Serve with tomato sauce and mustard.
Cornflake-crumbed chicken tenders with paprika. Anton mocks George's boat.

Season the flour, beat the eggs and mix the cornflakes with the paprika. Dip each tender in flour, egg, then cornflakes, and lay on a lined tray. Drizzle with oil and bake at 220C, turning once, until golden and cooked through. Stir the mayonnaise, honey and mustard together and serve as a dip.
M: Eleanor's Cajun meatloaf with mash and peas
Cajun meatloaf with mash and peas. Frederick says it's delicious.

Mix the mince, onion, capsicum, Cajun seasoning, breadcrumbs, egg, milk and salt with your hands. Shape into a loaf on a lined tray and brush with the tomato sauce mixed with the sugar. Bake at 180C for 1 hour, then rest for 10 minutes. Meanwhile boil the potatoes and mash with the butter and a splash of milk. Cook the peas, slice the meatloaf and serve with the mash.
125ml milk, plus a splash for the mash@Dairy
Buttery mash over a creamy fish pie. Snowbell: we do not eat family members.

Boil the potatoes and mash with the 40g butter and a splash of the milk. Melt the 50g butter, stir in the flour, then whisk in the rest of the milk and simmer until thick. Stir in the fish, prawns, peas and parsley, season and tip into a baking dish. Spread the mash over, scatter with cheese and bake at 200C until golden and bubbling.
600g firm white fish fillets, in chunks@Seafood
W: Ten inches tall chocolate layer cake
Tall chocolate layer cake with fudge icing, for Stuart feeling ten inches tall.

Whisk the flour, sugar, 60g cocoa, bicarb and a pinch of salt, then whisk in the eggs, buttermilk, oil and hot water. Divide between two lined 20cm tins and bake at 175C until a skewer comes out clean. Cool completely. Beat the butter with the icing sugar and 30g cocoa until fluffy, then sandwich and cover the cake.
60g cocoa powder, plus 30g for the frosting@Pantry
K: Fresh raspberry lemonade over ice, for Stuart winning George's boat race.
Simmer the raspberries, sugar and water for 5 minutes, then sieve and cool. Stir in the lemon juice, pour over ice and top with soda.
